value.body: A bioinformatics analyst uses software to analyse biological data such as DNA and RNA sequences and protein structures. Genomics and diagnostics companies, research institutes, and pharma and contract research firms hire them. A day involves running analysis pipelines, writing scripts, checking data quality and explaining results to lab scientists.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech Biotechnology or Bioinformatics; often an M.Sc / M.Tech

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Linux, Python or R, sequence databases and aligners

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Some freshers join genomics or diagnostics firms as bioinformatics trainees or associates, often after projects or internships that show programming and data skills. Many employers and most research labs prefer a master's degree.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Working on the Linux command line
Using sequence databases and alignment tools

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: senior bioinformatician, computational biologist, data scientist.
Research-heavy roles usually expect a master's or PhD.
Skills overlap with data science, which widens later options.

competition.note: B.Tech / B.E. (all branches) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
